operation_details.item: The user is lifelong lactose intolerant and avoids dairy milk, cheese, and cream.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I see you're planning a long afternoon of thesis writing. Are you thinking about coffee and snacks to keep your energy up?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Yes, exactly. I need something that will sustain me through several hours of focused work. Any recommendations for coffee and snacks that won't slow me down?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Great question. For sustained focus, I'd suggest a balanced snack with protein and complex carbs, plus a coffee that won't cause a crash. Do you have any dietary restrictions I should consider?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Good point. I am lifelong lactose intolerant and avoid dairy milk, cheese, and cream in my diet. So anything with dairy is out.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: I understand. That's a common and manageable restriction. For coffee, I'd recommend plant-based milk alternatives like almond, soy, or oat milk. Many cafés now offer these, and they froth well. For snacks, look for dairy-free options; many granola bars, nuts, and fruit are naturally safe. Always check ingredient labels for hidden dairy like whey or casein.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: That's helpful. What about something like a yogurt parfait? I know those usually have dairy, but are there dairy-free versions?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Yes, there are dairy-free yogurts made from coconut, soy, or almond milk. You could build a parfait with one of those, plus fresh berries and a sprinkle of granola. Just verify the granola doesn't contain dairy—some use butter or milk powder.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Perfect. I think I'll go with a latte made with oat milk and a side of almonds and an apple. That should keep me going. Do you have any tips for avoiding dairy in coffee creamers?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: For coffee creamers, stick with plant-based ones labeled 'dairy-free'—oat, soy, or coconut creamers are widely available. Avoid any that list 'cream' or 'milk' as an ingredient. If you're at a café, ask for a latte with oat milk and no whipped cream, which often contains dairy.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Thanks, I'll do that. Are there any hidden sources of lactose in common snacks I should watch out for?

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Absolutely. Watch for ingredients like whey, casein, lactoglobulin, and milk solids in chips, crackers, and even some dark chocolates. Chewing gum sometimes contains lactose as a binder. When in doubt, choose whole foods like fruits, vegetables, nuts, and seeds—they're naturally dairy-free.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Great advice. I'll stick with simple, whole foods and an oat milk latte. Thanks for helping me plan this out!

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: You're welcome. I hope you have a productive writing session. If you need any more tips on dairy-free eating or study snacks, feel free to ask.
